slides.title: Media, Technology, and News
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 7 English, Unit 8: Media, Technology, and News. This unit is called "Media, Technology, and News" because you will explore how information travels in the modern world and why it matters to think critically about everything you read, watch, and share. Every day, millions of messages flow through newspapers, television channels, websites, and social media platforms. Some of these messages are carefully researched and truthful. Others are misleading, exaggerated, or completely false. As a young person growing up in the digital age, one of the most important skills you can develop is the ability to tell the difference between reliable information and misinformation. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Explain what media literacy means and why it is important for young people today.
Identify the key features of a reliable news source and an unreliable one.
Read a text about media and answer comprehension and analysis questions in full sentences.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to explain what media literacy means and why it is important for young people today. You will also identify the key features of a reliable news source and an unreliable one. You will also read a text about media and answer comprehension and analysis questions in full sentences. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: express, claim, allege, correspond, explanation, influence. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Media Literacy: Reading the News with Care
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Media Literacy: Reading the News with Care and Breaking News at Kilima Academy. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Present Perfect + Just, and Reported Speech
bullets: The present perfect with just announces that something happened moments ago, which is why news reports say, "The government has just announced a new...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Present Perfect + Just, and Reported Speech. The present perfect with just announces that something happened moments ago, which is why news reports say, "The government has just announced a new policy." Reported speech then lets a journalist pass on what someone said without quoting every word. Together, these two patterns are the engine room of news English. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Debate: Digital Media Ethics. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
